subject.title: feat(onboard): recommendations store with once-semantics and self-naming bootstrap

question: Should onboarding recommendations be a single machine-wide, once-only shared offer that a first-run workspace bootstrap may consume and acknowledge, rather than state scoped to a workspace or agent?
rationale: The branch intentionally defines durable UX and state ownership for future onboarding runs; tests can verify mechanics but cannot select the permanent product scope or recovery expectation.

options.title: Approve the shared once-only contract
options.body: Keep the singleton shared-state record and three-step bootstrap once final-head fresh-install and re-run evidence is attached.

options.title: Scope recommendations per workspace or agent
options.body: Redesign the persistence key and acknowledgement flow before merge so independent workspaces do not share one consumed offer.

options.title: Defer the bootstrap integration
options.body: Land neither contract until the onboarding redesign owner specifies the permanent recommendation lifecycle and recovery UX.

recommendation.title: Approve the shared once-only contract
recommendation.body: Keep the singleton shared-state record and three-step bootstrap once final-head fresh-install and re-run evidence is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this person directly to the onboarding redesign plan and current implementation, making them the clearest available routing candidate for the intended UX contract.
